title: Priority-based hedging and graceful cache fallback for downstream resilience
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem statement:
We observe tail latency spikes and partial outages when regional Redis clusters or SQL read-replicas degrade under bursty write-heavy workloads. Current mitigation (simple retry + global failover) increases request cost and amplifies downstream load, sometimes causing cascading failures and violating 99p latency SLOs for the hosted API.

Goal:
Design and implement a priority-aware hedging and graceful cache-fallback system that: 1) classifies requests by tenant priority and SLO sensitivity, 2) attempts local fast-paths (KV cache, read replica) with short hedges to fallback targets, and 3) gracefully degrades non-critical traffic using connection-pool admission and token-based shedding to protect SLOs for P0/P1 tenants.

Scope and constraints:
- Targets: Redis (prefix/KV cache), Kafka consumer lag read paths, and primary/replica SQL queries.
- Must work cross-region: primary routing in region-of-origin, with probabilistic hedging to secondary regions when local latency exceeds threshold for P0 requests.
- No changes to user-visible API. Behavior controlled by routing/policy flags in config store and feature flags for canary rollout.
- Minimal CPU/GPU overhead; prefer lightweight algorithmic decisions over heavy orchestration.

Design summary:
1) Request classification: a small middleware that assigns "priority" (P0/P1/P2) and "sensitivity" (latency/consistency) based on route + tenant metadata. Defaults derived from billing tier + explicit manifest.
2) Short-circuit local cache: for read paths, attempt in-process prefix/KV cache (optimistic local read). If miss or KV deprioritized by policy, initiate primary downstream call.
3) Hedging windows: for P0 requests, send a parallel hedged request to a nearby region or to a lower-cost replica after T_hedge_ms (configurable; default 40ms). Only one hedge allowed per request. For P1, hedging disabled by default but can be enabled for canary tenants.
4) Circuit breakers + pool admission: per-downstream (redis/sql/kafka) token buckets control concurrent outstanding requests. When utilization above soft threshold, low-priority requests are short-circuited to a degraded path (cached stale result, or precomputed fallback) and admitted requests prioritized by token-lanes.
5) Graceful cache fallback: stale-while-revalidate semantics — if primary call fails or times out and an acceptable stale cache exists, return stale + spawn asynchronous refresh with backoff. Staleness bounds are per-route and per-tenant.
6) Observability & SLO mapping: expose metrics (hedge_rate, hedge_success_pct, stale_return_rate, pool_rejection_rate, per-tenant 99p latency) to Console with alerts when P0 SLOs drift.

Trade-offs considered:
- Hedging increases overall request volume; mitigated by limiting hedges to high-priority traffic and short windows.
- Returning stale data risks correctness; we keep strict per-route staleness limits and attach response headers to enable caller-informed behavior where possible.
- Multi-region hedging increases egress costs; adaptive policy will reduce hedging when cost budget is exceeded.

Acceptance criteria:
- P0 99p latency remains within target for simulated 2x burst load in region with 30% Redis error rate.
- Global error rate for core endpoints does not increase compared to baseline more than 0.5%.
- Rollout strategy available via feature flags and percent-based canary.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable on internal staging tenants + 5% production traffic for P0 routes; monitor hedging and stale-return metrics for 72h.
- Phase 2 (expand): adjust thresholds and extend to P1 if metrics are stable for 2 weeks.
- Phase 3: default enable with adaptive cost caps and auto-disable on region overload.

Runbook highlights:
- If P0 99p spikes: check hedging_success, pool_rejection_rate; if hedging success is low and pool rejection high, lower hedging and increase pool size or adjust admission policy.
- If stale_return_rate unexpectedly high: toggle feature flag to disable stale fallback for affected route and investigate upstream refresh latency.

Links to artifacts:
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/design/priority-hedge-cache-fallback (internal)
- Prototype benchmark: https://perf.redwood.ai/bench/ENG-77822-heap (grafana)

notes: Keep hedging disabled for tenant-level compliance modes until legal verifies cross-region egress. Consider KMS audit for any cross-region cache encryption keys.
